goal: Show-me day with the hook: the question 'What do we already know about a topic, and which book could tell us more?' and the topic named by word and a plain sunflower icon; the teacher thinks aloud filling the 'know' box first, then opens the picture of a sunflower taller than the teacher and draws one wonder, holding the unit's skill card.
note: Day 1 holds the hook, the question and the modeled sheet only; no retrieval and no readiness check (every row this unit assumes was used in kindergarten, so each opens as retrieval on a later day). Skill card: think, draw what I know, draw what I wonder, which book? Supplies: the sunflower picture, a large know and wonder sheet, crayons; the class sits on the carpet. Neutral topic. Topic first: the teacher names the topic by word and a plain icon (no detail), the class fills the 'know' box, and only then is the picture or book opened ('before you start looking', the owned id's order).

goal: Practice day: after putting the four cycle pictures in order and saying one 'I wonder' about the day's picture, pairs fill a know and wonder sheet on two new topics, each named by word and icon and its 'know' box filled before its picture is shown with the skill card in hand, and the teacher gives feedback on each 'know' (a real fact, not a guess or a wonder).
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: the four pictured cycle steps (ask, find, share, reflect) put in order and the card back on the wall, then one 'I wonder' about the day's picture (k-class-inquiry, k-wonder, kindergarten). Practice of the move modeled on day 1. The teacher reads last year's class-level note, where there is one, to plan the reteach. A child who prefers not to speak may point or whisper. No child is asked what they know from home. Topic first: the teacher names the topic by word and a plain icon (no detail), the class fills the 'know' box, and only then is the picture or book opened ('before you start looking', the owned id's order).

goal: Show-me day: for a question read aloud ('How tall do sunflowers grow?') the teacher thinks aloud choosing between a short sunflower story and a sunflower information book and says why the information book is more likely to answer, then the class fetches the information-book bin by its label.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: a child fetches the fact-book bin by its picture label (k-picture-book-labels, kindergarten). Lean: ELA grade 1 teaches books that tell stories and books that inform in unit 2 (weeks 7 to 15), later than this day; this day teaches the choice itself on two covers and a few pages, leaning on ELA for nothing. Supplies: the sunflower story and information book (Curio Class writes both), cover strips, the labeled class bins.

goal: Inquiry day: the class runs the cycle on the host or stand-alone question: the teacher names the topic and each child fills the 'know' box with the book still closed, then the wonder, the class chooses the information book, the teacher reads, each child checks one 'know' against the book and draws one found fact; share circle, where the class says the big idea of the read-aloud in one sentence; then the self-check.
note: Host: what the class knows about shadows and the sky (science:s1-sky-patterns, science grade 1 unit 1, weeks 1 to 4) or how a tree stays standing (science:s1-parts-mimic, unit 2, weeks 4 to 9); stand-alone: 'How tall do sunflowers grow?' with the sunflower read-aloud. No retrieval opening (k-wonder was retrieved on day 2). Skill card withdrawn today. The teacher copies the class's 'knows' onto an unnamed class know and wonder chart kept on the wall for the year-end reflect step (day 30). Kept Candidate, zero days: the big idea said orally at the share. A 'know' that turns out not quite right is praised as good checking, never corrected in front of the class. Whose voices: the unit records the makers of its read-aloud and pictures (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment on new cases: the topic (snails) named by word and a plain snail outline with no detail, the prompts read aloud, each child draws or writes one fact already known and one wonder on the sheet, and only then is the full snail picture shown; a story-or-information pointing strip for a named question, and a whisper walk on why the information book is the better choice.
note: About 17 minutes for 30: sheet item about 8 minutes (g1-what-i-know, marked from the page: a fact the icon does not show, true of the topic; the wonder box asks for a question, AASL.V.C.1); scanned pointing item about 2 minutes; whisper walk about 15 seconds a child, about 7 minutes (g1-story-or-fact-book). No skill card. Scored on the class checklist; sheets go home after marking. Response on day 6.

goal: Respond day: the self-check (point at the pictured step done well and say one thing to do better) and one new 'I wonder' for the board, then the regrouped reteach by the step missed on the checklist, ending with one fresh try on a new picture.
note: Self-check and new wonder about five minutes. Groups from the class checklist by the step missed (no real prior fact; no wonder; wrong book; no reason). The class practices a book-corner task while the adult works with one group. The unit's checklist is thrown away at the end of today.

goal: Show-me day with the hook: a big information book and the question 'Where in a book, or on the page our teacher opened, is the answer to our question?'; the teacher thinks aloud finding what tree roots do by the cover, the contents page, a heading, a picture and its label.
note: Day 1 of the unit: hook, question and the modeled search only. Skill card: look at the contents, find the heading, turn to the page, show it. Lean: ELA grade 1 teaches text features in unit 3 (weeks 16 to 24), later than this day; this day teaches the contents page and headings itself, as finding tools only. Supplies: the big information book on tree roots (Curio Class writes it).

goal: Practice day: after holding a question and raising a hand at the answering sentence, pairs find the answering page in three short mini-books by the contents page and headings, one of them a labeled picture or simple chart, and show the page to a partner.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: the class holds a question while the teacher reads, hands up at the answering sentence (k-listen-and-retell, kindergarten). Kept Candidate, zero days: reading information from a labeled picture or simple chart, with help, as one mini-book's answering page. Pairs hold the skill card. Supplies: three mini-books, contents sheets (Curio Class writes them).

goal: Show-me day on the class screen: only the page the teacher opened is used; the teacher says in one sentence what the internet is, then models the stop rule on pretend cases (a pop-up asking for a name, a picture that feels wrong: close it, tell the adult, no blame) and that we never type our name or school.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: point at the three stop pictures in order (k-library-visit, kindergarten). The teacher's page: the unit's tree-roots read-aloud page on the Curio Class site (the same page printed in the card frame on the paper path); any other page the teacher picks gets the teacher page's swap note (what was checked, and when). Device: the teacher's one shared class device, or the printed card frame and pretend screen cards (the paper path meets the move in full). No child types anything; pretend cases never show a real site. Sensitive ground items 2 and 3 (the stop rule, privacy): the teacher page says what the adult does if an upsetting picture ever appears and points to health's steps if a child tells something worrying. Kept Candidate, about 2 minutes: what the internet is, in one sentence.

goal: Inquiry day: the class runs the cycle on the host or stand-alone question: says what it knows and wonders, finds the answering page in a mini-book and on the teacher's page, each child draws and labels the fact, partner share, then the self-check.
note: Opening retrieval inside the ask step: a quick spoken know and wonder on the class question, said before any book or page is opened (g1-what-i-know, unit 1). Host: how a plant's parts help it (science:s1-parts-mimic, science grade 1 unit 2, weeks 4 to 9, just ended, so the class brings its tree questions back); stand-alone: 'What do tree roots do?' Skill card withdrawn today; the stop pictures stay on the wall. The teacher's page is the unit's tree-roots read-aloud page on the Curio Class site (printed in the card frame on the paper path); another page gets the swap note. Shared device or printed card frame; the stop rule on any screen. Whose voices: the unit records the makers of its read-aloud and pictures (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment on new cases: a printed contents page and a two-page spread from a mini-book not seen before, a question read aloud, each child circles the heading and the page number that answer it, then on a printed card-frame teacher's page on the same question circles the labeled picture that answers it; then the stop steps pointed in order for two pretend cases, and a whisper walk on what we never type.
note: About 18 minutes for 30: sheet item about 7 minutes (g1-find-in-a-book: heading and page number both circled); teacher's page item about 2 minutes (the labeled picture circled: a second kind of place, so the item asks all of the with-help slice of AASL.IV.B.1); scanned pointing item about 4 minutes (stop steps in order); whisper walk about 10 seconds a child, about 5 minutes (g1-device-stop-rule). No skill card. Response on day 12. Before the checklist is thrown away, the teacher writes a class count of who met each move on the mid-year check sheet (day 13).

goal: Respond day: partner shares of the inquiry drawings, then the regrouped reteach by the step missed (contents, heading, page number, the stop steps), ending with one fresh try on a new mini-book or pretend card.
note: Partner shares about five minutes. Groups from the checklist by the step missed; the rest of the class practices a book-corner task. The unit's checklist is thrown away today, after the class count is written.

goal: Mid-year course-level check, week 13, on new cases from unit 1 only: a know and wonder sheet on a new topic named by word and a plain icon, the full picture held back until the sheet is done, a story-or-information pointing strip for a named question, and a whisper walk on why; unit 2's end result is carried as the class count, not re-tested.
note: About 17 minutes for 30: sheet item about 8 minutes (g1-what-i-know, marked: a fact the icon does not show, true of the topic); pointing item about 2 minutes; whisper walk about 7 minutes (g1-story-or-fact-book). Unit 2 ended on day 11, so the check draws on unit 1 and repeats no task given in the last two weeks (the contents sheet, stop steps and never-type walk of day 11 are not used). New topic and covers, not the snail. No skill card. Response on day 14.

goal: Respond day for the mid-year check: the missed step retaught in small groups from the check's sheet, ending with one fresh try on a new picture or cover pair.
note: Groups by the step missed on the check sheet; the class practices sorting cover cards into story and information books in the book corner while the adult works with each group. Sheets go home after.

goal: Show-me day with the hook: the question 'How can a team find a fact, and say which book it came from?' and the three pictured job cards (finder, holder, teller); the teacher and two helpers act out each job on a bird picture while the teacher thinks aloud.
note: Day 1 of the unit: hook, question and the modeled jobs only. Skill card: finder, holder, teller; I found this in... by... Lean: ELA grade 1 unit 1 (weeks 1 to 7) taught building on others' talk, before this unit; the day uses the class's talk rules and teaches the turn with the job cards itself. Groups of three mixed by the teacher, never by background.

goal: Show-me day: after one group turn with the talking object, the teacher models the source line 'I found this in the book (title) by (author)' and copies a title and author from a cover onto a sticky note, and says that a found fact came from its maker, so we say where we found it.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: one group turn with the talking object, each child telling one fact, opening with the kindergarten turn card's two pictures in SEL's words, 'eyes look, wait my turn' (k-talk-in-group, kindergarten). Review of k-who-made-book inside the model: the maker's name on the cover. Kept Candidate, about 2 minutes: saying aloud that we name the maker of a fact we pass on, put as a habit to follow, never a warning. Sensitive ground item 4: a child who calls a found fact 'mine' is helped to say 'I found it in...', never corrected in front of the group. Supplies: cover cards, sticky notes.

goal: Practice day: after pointing to the maker's name on a cover card, groups take jobs on a new picture set, find a fact, swap jobs and find another; the teller uses the 'I found this in... by...' frame each time, with pairs holding the skill card.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: point to the maker's name on a cover card (k-who-made-book, kindergarten). Practice of the jobs (day 15) and the source line (day 16). A child who prefers not to speak may be finder or holder today; every child holds every job across the unit. Supplies: two picture sets, job cards, cover cards.

goal: Inquiry day: each group runs the cycle on the host or stand-alone question: finds a fact in a mini-book by its headings, the teller tells it with title and author, the sticky note goes on the group's drawing, the group says what its facts add up to and names what each helper added; then the self-check.
note: Opening retrieval inside the find step: the answering page found by contents and heading (g1-find-in-a-book, unit 2). Host: the shared research on a bird's body parts (ela:e1-shared-research, review, ELA grade 1 unit 3, weeks 16 to 24, in step); stand-alone: 'How do birds build their nests?' with the bird read-aloud. Skill card withdrawn today. Kept Candidate, zero days: the group says what its facts add up to at the share. Whose voices: the unit records the makers of its read-aloud and pictures (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment on new cases: stations of three at the check table with a new picture set, where each child, holding one card of the set, says one finding of their own and then names what one helper added, the jobs kept for handing and holding the cards; meanwhile the seated class copies the title and author from a new cover card at each seat onto a sticky note.
note: About 18 minutes for 30: one minute of instructions to the whole class; station of three, each child says a finding (about 15 seconds) and names a helper's part (about 10 seconds), about 1.7 minutes a group, ten groups, about 17 minutes (g1-group-helpers: every child speaking up with a finding, AASL.III.D.1, and naming what a helper added, AASL.II.A.1); the sticky-note copy is the seated task during the stations (g1-author-and-title, marked from the note afterwards: both title and author copied so a reader could find the book; spelling help allowed). Response on day 20.

goal: Respond day: a share of the groups' drawings, then the regrouped reteach by the step missed (title, author, a job, naming a helper's part), ending with one fresh try.
note: Share about five minutes. Groups from the checklist; the class practices a book-corner task. The unit's checklist is thrown away today.

goal: Show-me day with the hook: a finished class information book from a pretend class and the question 'What can our class find out together, and how do we make each page better?'; the teacher thinks aloud through one page of the template (a labeled drawing, one sentence of a found fact, a source line).
note: Day 1 of the unit: hook, question and the modeled page only. Skill card: find one fact, draw it, label it, say where it came from; one star, one wish. Lean: ELA grade 1 unit 2 (weeks 7 to 15) ran a shared research and writing project before this unit; ELA's writing goes further, this unit teaches the page itself. Supplies: the pretend class book, page templates on heavier paper.

goal: Inquiry day: after a know and wonder sheet on the class topic, the teacher shows a picture menu of 6 to 8 wonders the source set answers, including any class wonders that match; each child picks one, their own where it is on the menu, and finds the answering page in the class's source set by the contents page and headings.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: the know and wonder sheet on the class topic (g1-what-i-know, unit 1); the find step brings back g1-find-in-a-book (unit 2). Host: how animal parents help their young (science:s1-parent-offspring, science grade 1 unit 7, weeks 24 to 26, later than this day); bridge from the frame's 'if later' line: the class asks and finds from the animal-parents read-aloud (stand-alone question 'How do animal parents keep their babies fed and warm?'), and science's unit then meets pages already drafted; where a school runs that science unit earlier, the class uses it. The source set is written so each menu wonder has one answering page, so every child has a found fact by day 23. Case set keeps to feeding and warmth (birds, penguins, kangaroos), never a hunt or a lost young one. Whose voices: the unit records the makers of its read-aloud and pictures (C12).

goal: Inquiry day: after saying a source line for a found fact, each child drafts a page: a labeled drawing of the found fact, one sentence written or dictated, and a sticky-note source line copied from the book's cover.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: 'I found this in... by...' said for a fact (g1-author-and-title, unit 3). Skill card in hand today (the first page drafted). No family photo or family fact goes in the book. Sentences may be dictated to the adult. Supplies: page templates, crayons, sticky notes.

goal: Show-me day: after putting the four cycle pictures in order, the teacher models a star (one thing a pretend page does well, such as a clear label) and a wish (one thing to add) with the pictured frame, specific and kind, not 'I like it', and shows that the maker may say no to a wish.
note: Opening retrieval, five minutes: the four cycle pictures in order (k-class-inquiry, kindergarten; both unit 4 rows build on it). Kind feedback: the star comes first, wishes are about the page, never the child; the teacher models on a pretend page before any pair work. Supplies: the star-and-wish frame, pretend pages.

goal: Inquiry day: in pairs, each child gives a classmate's draft one star and one wish with the pictured frame, then each maker chooses whether to use the wish and revises their own page.
note: Kept Candidate, zero days: beginning to respond to feedback to revise. The frame calls this day 'practice'; it is Application here because each maker revises a page (GLOSSARY, teaching day). Skill card withdrawn today. Pairs set by the teacher; the maker may say no to a wish and say why.

goal: End-of-unit assessment on new cases: the teacher reads a short passage not heard before twice with a held question, and each child draws and labels one fact that answers it and writes or dictates one sentence; then each child draws a star by one thing done well on a pretend classmate's page, and in a whisper walk says 'This page taught me ___' and one wish.
note: About 18 minutes for 30: sheet item about 9 minutes (g1-class-book: the fact answers the question; a product standing for AASL.I.B.3); star on the pretend page, sheet item about 2 minutes; whisper walk about 15 seconds a child, about 7 minutes ('This page taught me ___': responding to what a classmate's work says, AASL.I.C.1; the wish, g1-star-and-wish: about the work and doable, AASL.I.C.2). No skill card. Response on day 27. Before the checklist is thrown away, a class count goes on the year-end check sheet.

goal: Respond day: the teacher reads each page's sentence of the class information book and each child tells a partner one thing a friend's page taught them, then the self-check by pointing and the regrouped reteach by the step missed, ending with one fresh try.
note: The teacher reads each page's sentence, about 6 minutes; partner telling, about 2 minutes; self-check by pointing, about 2 minutes; reteach and fresh try, about 9 minutes. Kept Candidate, zero class days: the class book may go home in turn so families read it, by the school's own rules (family note). Supplies: yarn or staples to bind the book. The unit's checklist is thrown away today, after the class count is written.

goal: Year-end course-level check, week 28, on new cases from units 1 to 3, all sheet and pointing items: circle the heading and page number on a printed contents page, copy a new cover's title and author onto a sticky note, a know and wonder sheet on a new topic named by word and a plain icon, and point at the stop steps in order for a pretend case; unit 4 is carried as the class count.
note: About 18 minutes for 30: contents page about 5 minutes (unit 2; g1-find-in-a-book alone, one source, so ~AASL.IV.B.1 is not claimed here; day 11 holds it); sticky note about 4 minutes (unit 3); know and wonder sheet about 7 minutes (unit 1; marked: a fact the icon does not show); stop steps about 2 minutes (unit 2). Unit 4 was assessed on day 26, so the check draws on units 1 to 3 and repeats no task form given in the last two weeks (day 26's passage page and star-and-wish are not used). Every item read aloud. No skill card. Response on days 29 and 30.

goal: Respond day 1 for the year-end check: the gaps retaught in small groups from the check's sheet, ending with one fresh try on a new case.
note: Groups by the step missed on the sheet; the class practices a book-corner task. Sheets go home after.

goal: Respond day 2, the year's reflect step: the class reads its information book again, each child compares one 'know' from the unnamed class chart made in unit 1 with what they know now, says one step they now do well and one wonder they still have, while the teacher takes a last try with any child the reteach did not reach.
note: The class book is reread, not made, so g1-class-book is not claimed today. Uses the unnamed class know and wonder chart from day 4 (the sheets went home). The teacher writes a class-level note for the grade 2 teacher of the moves the class needs again, never a per-child record (the checklist rule).
